briefing.headline: OpenAI and DeepSeek race toward AGI thresholds as US export controls tighten on advanced chips

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AI frontier has accelerated with new model releases from OpenAI and xAI, while regulatory pressure mounts on compute exports. Safety concerns persist amid rapid deployment cycles.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI unveiled o4-preview with enhanced multi-agent coordination. Anthropic's Claude 4.5 and Google's Gemini 3.0 show gains in reasoning, while Meta open-sourced Llama 4 and DeepSeek released R1-2026 closing the performance gap.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New NIST guidelines emphasize runtime monitoring for agentic systems.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: TSMC broke ground on three new 2nm fabs dedicated to AI accelerators. Microsoft and xAI announced joint 500MW data center clusters in Texas, while NVIDIA's Blackwell ramp faces continued supply constraints.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will the first ASI system emerge from a US lab or a Chinese state-backed consortium by 2028?
